name: com.stocklens/stocklens
title: StockLens
description: Where a company stands in its market and why. The largest companies in each market need no account.

tools.name: add_to_watchlist
tools.description: Add one company to one of the person's StockLens portfolios as a company they follow, so its score stays readable here. Call it only when the person has asked for it, or agreed to an offer a StockLens result supplied in next_step; a yes to an offer you composed yourself is not agreement. Without portfolio_id or portfolio_name it adds to the default portfolio, and the result names the portfolio that received it. Relay the result's message, which says where the company went. A status other than added is an answer, not an error: relay its message and act on next_step. After an add the person accepted from a get_market_summary offer, call get_market_summary again to answer their question. One ticker per call; for a list of companies, use add_to_watchlist_batch. It does not trade, record a holding or move money.

ticker.description: Stock ticker symbol (e.g. AAPL). Exactly one ticker per call.

exchange.description: Exchange code (e.g. NASDAQ). Optional. Resolved automatically if omitted.

portfolio_id.description: The id of the portfolio to add to, as get_portfolio_insights lists it. Optional: without it or portfolio_name the company goes to the default portfolio.

portfolio_name.description: The name of the portfolio to add to, as the person names it (exact, case does not matter). Optional.

tools.name: add_to_watchlist_batch
tools.description: Add a list of companies the person gave you, up to 100 rows, to one of their StockLens portfolios, in two calls. First call with confirm false: nothing is added and every row returns its outcome. Relay summary_line and message, then every row that is not a plain add, grouped by outcome, and name the plain adds in one line; name the portfolio only when portfolio_count is above 1. Ask which rows to add. Then call with confirm true, the preview_id, the same rows, the same portfolio and the confirmed_indexes the person approved. Send only rows the person gave you. For an ambiguous row, ask which listing using its candidates; never pick one. Add a not_covered row only if the person asks for it. A changed list or a different portfolio needs a new preview; preview_mismatch means the preview expired or no longer matches, so preview again. Without portfolio_id or portfolio_name it uses the default portfolio. It does not trade, record holdings or move money.

query.description: One company as the person wrote it: a ticker (AAPL), a listing (SHOP.TO) or a company name.

rows.description: The companies the person gave you, one per row, in their order. Never add a row they did not name.

confirm.description: false previews the list and adds nothing. true adds the rows of confirmed_indexes from the preview that preview_id names.

preview_id.description: The preview_id the preview returned. Required when confirm is true.

confirmed_indexes.description: The index of every row the person approved, from the preview. Required when confirm is true.

portfolio_id.description: The id of the portfolio to add to, as get_portfolio_insights lists it. Optional: without it or portfolio_name the list goes to the default portfolio.

portfolio_name.description: The name of the portfolio to add to, as the person names it (exact, case does not matter). Optional.

tools.name: discover_stocks
tools.description: Screen the companies StockLens scores nightly by region, exchange, sector, industry, market-cap band and trading volume, sorted by one of the six StockLens scores or by market cap, volume or ticker, and return the top or bottom N. Every list is computed inside one listing market: the one named in macro_in or exchange_in, otherwise the United States, and market and market_name in the result name it, so always say which market the rows are from, and when the person named no market, that others are covered, without screening them. For another market the person asks for (US, CA, EU, CH, GB, JP), call again naming it; never merge or compare lists across markets. multiple_markets and market_not_covered mean nothing was ranked: relay message. There is no popularity ordering; ask the person to choose another. Use it for any top, best, worst or filtered list, never one built from get_market_summary or general knowledge. To compare only companies the person names, call get_shortlist_summary instead. It has no valuation, price-target or growth filter; say so rather than calling a score sort one. status ranked means the requested order was used. When a ranked result carries message, relay it; it states what the ranking covers, so never present the rows as a ranking of more than that. browse_substituted means a score order was asked for and market-cap order with scores hidden was returned, so never describe those rows as ranked by score. locked means no companies are named; relay message verbatim. access_tier and reach_capped_at say what the caller can sort and how far; signed_in_as names their account. Report every returned row in its actual order and retain the population and access/substitution message. Where reading_ref and inspection are supplied, inspect only the company the person asks about; never fetch every row. When findings is present, explain findings.leading, then findings.first_answer, instead of key_drivers, as findings.claim allows: strongest, they moved this score most; strongest_first, the first moved it most and the second is another factor; explained, describe what the available evidence shows, with no biggest-mover sentence. Give a finding's fact figure with its own period, which can differ from the reading's date and from another finding's. A next look is findings.next_looks[0], or the second when the first's topic was already covered for this company in the conversation or misses the person's ask; skip both when both were covered, and never mention the one you do not ask. When the person asks directly for a figure a next look carries, give it with its period, then end with the other next look's question if it is still new. Otherwise ask that one question, in its words or your own, as the answer's final line, after any link. Never state, round or hint at any figure from next_looks before the person says yes. On a yes, give only its answer as given (the company figure with its period, and for a comparison the peer figure, statistic and group), without another call and without computing anything from the figures, then stop: no other offer, menu, save or analysis. After that answer, end with the other next look's question if it is still new; otherwise stop. A finding's qualification speaks only of that trailing P/E reading: when applied is true, say in the same sentence that the company's qualifying_measure of company_figure (trailing period to period_end) eased how StockLens weighed its P/E of pe_figure against peer_median for peer_group (a blended peer mark when peer_basis is blended, never a median of companies), and how it still reads there (remaining_assessment); when applied is false, mention the figure only as context, never as easing anything, whatever the finding's own label says. When qualifying_ref names another finding in the answer, it is the same figure: say it once, keeping both findings. Never present it as a change to the overall score or a view of the stock as a whole. For a finding tied to a source, give its event_date with the event (On the Oct 29 earnings call, In its Nov 8 filing; add the year across a year boundary). An insider transaction uses its trade date. For measured activity name the event_window_start and event_window_end, never a single latest article, filing or trade. Only the current result's dated reasons and questions qualify. Never substitute the reading's date or bring an undated, stale or future event into a reason or question. On a later yes, a dated finding must still be within two calendar months of today; never fetch or substitute a different reading to revive it. Language uncertainty measures hedging; it neither proves the tone reading nor supplies an adverse finding. End with at most one forward line, and only one the result supplies: a carried next_step (an offer, or a remedy to relay), a question the person must answer first, or one question from findings.next_looks as the findings rule says. Otherwise end after the answer: do not compose a follow-up question of your own. Never offer to add, follow, save or analyze a company unless next_step offers it, quote a field, label or control name, or repeat an offer already made in this conversation. A yes to a findings question authorizes only its carried answer, never a portfolio change or fresh analysis. One forward line serves the whole list; at most one row carries next_looks. A successful result counts once toward the person's weekly research allowance; a RATE_LIMITED result states the limit and when it renews, so relay it and do not call again before then.

macro_in.description: Listing market to rank in, where the companies list: US, CA, EU, CH, GB or JP. Every answer is computed inside one listing market, the one named here or by exchange_in, otherwise the United States, and market and market_name in the result say which. For another market, name it, for example JP. Several markets in one call are refused: call once per market and never merge the lists.

exchange_in.description: Restrict to these exchanges, all inside one listing market. Every answer is computed inside one listing market, the one these exchanges or macro_in belong to, otherwise the United States, and market and market_name in the result say which. Exchanges of different markets are refused: call once per market.

sector_in.description: Restrict to these GICS sectors. Omitted = no restriction.

industry_in.description: Restrict to these GICS industries. Omitted = no restriction.

market_cap_band.description: Restrict to this market-cap band. Omitted = no cap restriction.

volume_floor.description: Minimum average trading volume. Omitted = no floor.

sort_by.description: One of the 6 StockLens scores, market_cap, volume or ticker. Default composite_score. Popularity ordering is unavailable.

direction.description: top = highest first, bottom = lowest first. Default top.

limit.description: Number of matches to return (the N in top/bottom N), 1 to 100. Default 10.

search_text.description: Free-text company name/ticker search, up to 80 characters.

In that state, or when narrative.status is pending or running, call again right away at most twice more, then relay message and stop until the person asks. A failed status is an answer; relay error_message. A complete result is the saved report: the composite score and rating word, the evidence word (Full, Core or Low), each domain's score, grade word and contribution (cornerstone, major, supporting or contextual), its key_drivers (up to three, each with its evidence), lens and domain_coverage, and its written summaries (domain conclusions, synthesis, key strengths and challenges) at either depth once narrative.status is ready. Until then relay message: pending or running means they are still being written, and you may briefly summarize the scores and evidence supplied but never write a summary, cause or reason the result does not contain; failed means they could not be completed, and the scores and evidence stand. Preserve every material qualification; do not repeat bound findings as additional independent reasons. Open with the score, rating word, evidence word and the lens it was read through (time_range_display and analysis_focus_display); then synthesis_report in its written order (The Punch Line, Key Drivers, Primary Counterpoint); then the domains by contribution, cornerstone and major first with their conclusions, supporting and contextual briefly; then strengths and challenges. When result.findings is present, it gives this report's score reasons under its own horizon and analysis focus: use it in place of key_drivers, after the synthesis_report story, never instead of The Punch Line, Key Drivers or Primary Counterpoint. Bold each company's score and rating word where the answer first gives them. tools.name: get_portfolio_insights
tools.description: Read one of the person's StockLens portfolios: every company, holding or watching, with its score, rating word, market and Fundamental standing in that market, its largest sector share and its 7-night movers, each with its market and a same-direction driver from its latest reading. A one-market portfolio adds that market's average score, rating word and change over 7 and 30 nights; across markets, scores are not on one scale, so there is no average: relay scale_note and markets. Without portfolio_id or portfolio_name it reads the default portfolio. portfolios lists every portfolio the person owns and appears only when there is more than one: then name the portfolio you read once and offer the others by name. With one portfolio, never name it. A portfolio the person does not own returns portfolio_not_found with the choices; never guess. Relay message, caption, trust and concentration as written. If a window says insufficient_data, say so; do not estimate a change. config_changed marks a scoring-method change inside a window. The scores are the ones get_market_summary serves, as of as_of. To rank or screen other companies, call discover_stocks. No money figures, no personal advice. For a mover's dated source give its event_date or the measured window, never the reading's date. A successful result counts once toward the person's weekly research allowance; a RATE_LIMITED result states the limit and when it renews, so relay it and do not call again before then.

portfolio_id.description: The id of the portfolio to read, as a portfolios list gives it. Optional: without it or portfolio_name the default portfolio is read.

portfolio_name.description: The name of the portfolio to read, as the person names it (exact, case does not matter). Optional.

tools.name: initiate_analysis
tools.description: Start a fresh StockLens analysis of one company, only when the person asks for one or agrees to an offer of one in a get_market_summary result. A new run may use one Analysis credit, or one Plus Analysis credit when depth is plus; the result says if the person's plan does not include it. Use inspect_reading for already-produced evidence when its exact reference is available; an evidence question alone never authorizes a run. Both depths include written domain summaries and synthesis when produced; Plus adds deeper synthesis and extra web cards where available. The assistant result is condensed; the saved web report has the factor cards and Explain views. It waits up to 9 seconds for the analysis's scores and returns them in result with its analysis_id when they are ready, otherwise its analysis_id and current status. When there is no result, or narrative.status is pending or running, call fetch_analysis_result with that analysis_id right away; it waits for what is still being written. new_run_started says whether a new run started; present an existing one as the person's analysis, with its date. Present a returned result as fetch_analysis_result describes. One ticker per call. It does not rank or compare companies, and does not trade or move money.

ticker.description: Stock ticker symbol (e.g. AAPL). Exactly one ticker per call.

exchange.description: Exchange code (e.g. NASDAQ). Optional. Resolved automatically if omitted.

time_range.description: Intended holding period, looking forward from the analysis date. Shorter horizons give recent price action, momentum and news more emphasis than longer ones; longer horizons give business fundamentals and quality more emphasis. Input history can span longer periods. Does not predict price or returns. One window per calibrated band: short_2_wk (Short-term), medium_1_mo (Medium-term), long_1_yr (Long-term). Default medium_1_mo. The legacy medium_2_mo and long_2_yr aliases are still accepted and resolve to medium_1_mo and long_1_yr respectively.

analysis_focus.description: Analysis focus: low=Defensive, medium=Balanced, high=Growth. Default medium. Reweights downside/quality risk versus growth/fundamentals, never the underlying facts. Not a personal risk or suitability assessment.

risk_tolerance.description: Deprecated compatibility alias for analysis_focus. Use analysis_focus for new calls. If both are supplied they must agree (case-insensitive).

evidence_history_family.description: Optional. SHORT_HISTORY | MEDIUM_HISTORY | LONG_HISTORY. Must agree with the family implied by time_range (short_2_wk->SHORT_HISTORY, medium_1_mo/medium_2_mo->MEDIUM_HISTORY, long_1_yr/long_2_yr->LONG_HISTORY); a mismatch is rejected as a validation error before any credit is consumed. Does not select a representative range on its own.

analysis_emphasis.description: Optional. RISK_EMPHASIS | BALANCED | FUNDAMENTAL_GROWTH_EMPHASIS. Must agree with the emphasis implied by analysis_focus (low->RISK_EMPHASIS, medium->BALANCED, high->FUNDAMENTAL_GROWTH_EMPHASIS); a mismatch is rejected as a validation error before any credit is consumed.

depth.description: Analysis depth: standard or plus. Both include written domain summaries and synthesis when produced. Plus uses deeper synthesis and adds extra cards in the web report where available. Standard uses an Analysis credit (LENS_AI); Plus uses a Plus Analysis credit (LENS_AI_PLUS). Default standard.

tools.name: inspect_reading
tools.description: Explain why an exact StockLens reading says something, using evidence already produced; no credits, new analysis or writes. Use for a selected score reason, finding, qualification or assessment, including momentum, authorized moat or Beneish where produced. Copy reading_ref and the labelled view/selector from inspection arguments; overview is the default. A clear evidence request authorizes this read without another permission question. Follow a returned overview continuation only when more saved choices are needed; each call reads this same exact reading. Keep the company, date, reading kind/depth and all material context. USED_IN_ASSESSMENT, RELATED_OBSERVATION and FUTURE_CHECK have different roles. A selected_reason SOURCE_METRIC supplies its own saved interpretation; RELATED_ASSESSMENT is context, not evidence for that reason. Narrative sentences stay unbound. A standalone observation has no assessment-relative role; produced inapplicability can be inspected for its explanation, without a calculated score. Assessment-level unions do not prove per-sentence witnesses, a group is not a causal pair, and shared observations are not independent corroboration. Unknown, gated, expired and uncaptured detail stays typed; never substitute today's reading, retry unchanged or start a run to fill it. Pending/failed narrative does not erase deterministic evidence. Avoid repeating the same bound meaning as both narrative and finding. Only the four declared views are supported; this is not full structural inspection of every web card. An exact report link is optional. On request give the original dated evidence as history. Never offer an unsupported source as a current reason or question; only use supplied reading references and selectors.

reading_ref.description: Exact reading_ref returned by StockLens. Never reconstruct from a ticker or date.

view.description: Copy from inspection.arguments; default overview. Only overview, finding, assessment or observation.

selector.description: Copy the selector from inspection.arguments, including an optional overview continuation. Required for other views.

tools.name: remove_from_watchlist
tools.description: Remove one company from one of the person's StockLens portfolios. Call it only when the person has asked for it. Without portfolio_id or portfolio_name it removes from the default portfolio, and the result names the portfolio. Relay the result's message. A status other than removed is an answer, not an error. A holding with recorded transactions is not removed here; the result says where to do it. One ticker per call. It does not trade or delete transactions.

ticker.description: Stock ticker symbol (e.g. AAPL). Exactly one ticker per call.

exchange.description: Exchange code (e.g. NASDAQ). Optional. When omitted, the ticker is matched against the portfolio; if it is there on more than one exchange you will be asked which.

portfolio_id.description: The id of the portfolio to remove from, as get_portfolio_insights lists it. Optional: without it or portfolio_name the default portfolio is used.

portfolio_name.description: The name of the portfolio to remove from, as the person names it (exact, case does not matter). Optional.
